facts.text: Kilbourne began as a community when West Carroll Parish was created on March 26 1877, splitting Carroll Parish to resolve disputes over the parish seat.
Early settlers near Bayou Macon used the waterway to haul cotton and other goods to river ports, making it a natural transportation route.
Kilbourne was formally incorporated as a village in 1954 under Louisiana's Lawrason Act, a statute that enabled rural communities to organize local governance.
The village’s early growth relied on cotton plantations and timber harvesting, but its isolation limited rapid development until roads and mills were built.
Archaeological digs along Bayou Macon have uncovered Native American mounds, indicating pre‑colonial human activity long before European settlement.
Kilbourne sits close to the Arkansas state line and the Mississippi River, placing it near two major geographic boundaries within West Carroll Parish.
